anchor.exact: the Ainu linguistic lineage is originally not native at all to the ethnic territory of the historical Ainu but was relocated from Honshu in connection with the expansion of the Satsumon culture.

statement.en: The Ainu linguistic lineage is originally not native to the ethnic territory of the historical Ainu, having relocated from Honshu in connection with the expansion of the Satsumon culture.
statement.ja: アイヌ語の言語系統は歴史的なアイヌの民族領域に本来自生したものではなく、擦文文化の拡大に伴って本州から移転したものである。

entailment.quote: the Ainu linguistic lineage is originally not native at all to the ethnic territory of the historical Ainu but was relocated from Honshu in connection with the expansion of the Satsumon culture.

anchor.exact: This process involved a chain of language shifts which ultimately left Ainu as the only survivor of the original linguistic diversity of Jōmon Japan.

statement.en: A chain of language shifts ultimately left Ainu as the sole survivor of the original linguistic diversity of Jōmon Japan.
statement.ja: 一連の言語交替の過程により、最終的にアイヌ語は縄文時代の日本列島がもっていた本来の言語的多様性の唯一の生き残りとなった。

entailment.quote: a chain of language shifts which ultimately left Ainu as the only survivor of the original linguistic diversity of Jōmon Japan.

anchor.exact: A proto-form of this language, Proto-Ainu (Proto-Kurilic), which underlies the historically documented diversity of all the Ainu (Kurilic) varieties, was spoken on Hokkaido at the time of the Satsumon culture, probably less than 1000 but more than 500 years ago.

statement.en: Proto-Ainu (Proto-Kurilic) was spoken on Hokkaido during the period of the Satsumon culture, between approximately 500 and 1,000 years ago.

entailment.quote: was spoken on Hokkaido at the time of the Satsumon culture, probably less than 1000 but more than 500 years ago.

anchor.exact: This language was not original to Hokkaido, but had been relocated from Honshu, where its ancestral forms had been spoken since, at least, the Jōmon period, and where its presence clearly precedes the arrival of the Japanese (Japonic) lineage from the continent.

statement.en: Proto-Ainu was not originally native to Hokkaido, but was relocated from Honshu, where ancestral forms of the language had been spoken since at least the Jōmon period and preceded the arrival of Japonic.
statement.ja: 祖アイヌ語は元来北海道にあったものではなく、少なくとも縄文時代以降その祖先形態が話され、大陸からの日琉語族の到来より明らかに先行していた本州から移入されたものである。

entailment.quote: This language was not original to Hokkaido, but had been relocated from Honshu, where its ancestral forms had been spoken since, at least, the Jōmon period, and where its presence clearly precedes the arrival of the Japanese (Japonic) linea

anchor.exact: the first entity to have branched off was Sakhalin Ainu (Murayama 1971: 352; Vovin 1993: 157), which started diverging perhaps some 800 years ago, followed by Northern Kuriles Ainu less than 600 years ago.

anchor.exact: Ainu has several very early Japanese (Japonic) loanwords, including items like sippo ‘salt’ and pasuy ‘chopstick’, which preserve Old Japanese and/or Pre-Old-Japanese features (the stop pronunciation of ✶p, the diphthongoid sequence ✶uy)

anchor.exact: Ainu and Ghilyak show traces of relatively early lexical interaction, as in the case of Ainu tunakay ‘reindeer’ (→ Japanese tonakai) ← Pre-Proto-Ghilyak ✶tola-ŋa.y ‘pulling animal’ > modern Sakhalin Ghilyak tlaŋi (Austerlitz 1976).

statement.ja: アイヌ語 tunakay「トナカイ」はギリヤーク語（ニヴフ語）との初期の語彙接触を反映しており、プレ祖ギリヤーク語 *tola-ŋa.y「引く動物」からの借用である。

entailment.quote: Ainu and Ghilyak show traces of relatively early lexical interaction, as in the case of Ainu tunakay ‘reindeer’ (→ Japanese tonakai) ← Pre-Proto-Ghilyak ✶tola-ŋa.y ‘pulling animal’
